source.title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials

accepted.question_text: Let P(z) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 over C whose Hessian matrix Hes P is nilpotent, so P is Hessian nilpotent. Let Delta be the Laplace operator on C[z], Delta = sum from i = 1 to n of D_i squared. Must the iterated Laplacians of the powers of P eventually vanish, meaning Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large m?
accepted.context_brief: Vanishing Conjecture for degree-4 Hessian nilpotent polynomials

evidence.quote: A polynomial or formal power series P (z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := (d^2P/dz_i dz_j) are nilpotent.

Conjecture 1.1. (Vanishing Conjecture) Let Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 be the Laplace operator of C[z]. Then, for any HN polynomial P (z) (of homogeneous of degree d = 4), Delta^m P^{m+1} (z) = 0 when m >> 0.

accepted.question_text: Let P(z) be a formal power series in C[[z]] with order at least 2 and with (Hes P)(0) nilpotent. Define its symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z); when the inverse has the form G(z) = z + grad Q(z), call Q(z) the inversion pair of P(z). If P is self-inverting, meaning Q(z) = P(z), must every such self-inverting polynomial or formal power series be Hessian nilpotent?
accepted.context_brief: Whether self-inverting series are automatically Hessian nilpotent

evidence.quote: there exists a unique Qt (z) in C[[t]][[z]] with o(Qt (z)) >= 2 such that Gt (z) = z + t grad Qt (z). We call Qt (z) the deformed inversion pair of P (z).
Definition 4.1. A formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] with o(P (z)) >= 2 and (Hes P )(0) nilpotent is said to be self-inverting if its inversion pair Q(z) = P (z).
Open Problem 4.8. (a) Decide whether or not all self-inverting polynomials or formal power series are HN.

accepted.question_text: Classify all self-inverting polynomials and formal power series P(z) over C, where self-inverting means that P(z) has order at least 2, (Hes P)(0) is nilpotent, and the inversion pair Q(z) associated with the symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z) satisfies Q(z) = P(z). In particular, classify the Hessian nilpotent self-inverting examples.
accepted.context_brief: Classification of Hessian nilpotent self-inverting series

evidence.quote: Definition 4.1. A formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] with o(P (z)) >= 2 and (Hes P )(0) nilpotent is said to be self-inverting if its inversion pair Q(z) = P (z).
It is unknown if all HN self-inverting polynomials or formal power series can be obtained by the construction above.
Open Problem 4.8. (b) Classify all (HN) self-inverting polynomials and formal power series.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails? Equivalently, can one find a non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C for which Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) does not vanish for all sufficiently large m, or prove that no such example exists?
accepted.context_brief: Possible failure of the Vanishing Conjecture for non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent series

evidence.quote: One interesting question is whether or not the VC fails (as the JC does) for any HN formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] but P (z) not in C[z]? To our best knowledge, no such counterexample has been known yet.
Open Problem 5.2. Find a HN formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] but P (z) not in C[z], if there are any, such that the VC fails for P (z).

accepted.question_text: Let P(z) be a formal power series in C[[z]] with order o(P(z)) at least 2, and let Delta be the Laplace operator. If the sequence Delta^m(P(z)^m) eventually vanishes, meaning Delta^m(P(z)^m) = 0 for all sufficiently large m, must P(z) be Hessian nilpotent?
accepted.context_brief: Eventual vanishing of Delta^m P^m versus Hessian nilpotency

evidence.quote: A polynomial or formal power series P (z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := (d^2P/dz_i dz_j) are nilpotent.
Conjecture 6.4. Let P (z) in C[[z]] with o(P (z)) >= 2. If Delta^m P^m (z) = 0 for m >> 0, then P (z) is HN.

accepted.question_text: Let C^n carry the standard C-bilinear form <., .>, and let X(C^n) be the set of isotropic vectors alpha with <alpha, alpha> = 0. Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2 over C written as P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h_{alpha_i}(z)^d, where h_alpha(z) = <alpha, z> and each alpha_i lies in X(C^n). Define the graph G(P) to have vertex set {1, 2, ..., k}, with vertices i and j joined by an edge exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> is nonzero; regard G(P) as labeled when an edge i--j is assigned the value <alpha_i, alpha_j>, and in the even-degree variant when the edge label is h_{alpha_i}(z)^((d-2)/2) <alpha_i, alpha_j> h_{alpha_j}(z)^((d-2)/2). What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) ensure that P(z) is Hessian nilpotent?

evidence.quote: set h_beta (z) := <beta, z> and beta D := <beta, D>, where <., .> is the standard C-bilinear form of Cn. Let X(Cn) denote the set of all isotropic elements of Cn
We fix a homogeneous harmonic polynomial P (z) in C[z] of degree d >= 2, and assume that P (z) is given by Eq. (8.2) for some alpha_i in X(Cn) (1 <= i <= k).
The set of vertices of G(P ) will be the set of positive integers [k] := {1, 2, . . . , k}. The vertices i and j of G(P ) are connected by an edge iff <alpha_i , alpha_j> != 0.
we may also label edges of G(P ) by assigning <alpha_i , alpha_j> or (h_{alpha_i}^{(d-2)/2} <alpha_i , alpha_j> h_{alpha_j}^{(d-2)/2}), when d is even
Open Problem 8.4. (a) Find some necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P ) such that the homogeneous harmonic polynomial P (z) is HN.
